harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (10.100.254.10) as the cluster's internal NTP time source using chrony with `local stratum 10` (self-referenced, since outbound internet NTP is blocked in this environment) and `allow 10.100.254.0/24` to serve the cluster subnet. Configured node2 (10.100.254.11) to sync exclusively against node1 via `server 10.100.254.10 iburst prefer` in chrony.conf, with public ubuntu.pool.ntp.org entries removed on both nodes and systemd-timesyncd disabled in favor of chrony. Verified node2 achieved active sync (`^*`) to node1 at stratum 11 and node1 recorded NTP client requests from node2. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes: captured boot_id/uptime/service baselines, restarted each node via native `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and confirmed chrony auto-restarted and node2 automatically re-synced to node1 post-reboot on both occasions, preserving the internal time hierarchy.
actions_performed: Inspected OS and existing time-sync state on node1 and node2 (Ubuntu 24.04, systemd-timesyncd active, chrony absent)
Installed chrony via apt on node1 and node2
Confirmed outbound NTP/internet is blocked (curl to ntp.ubuntu.com timed out), motivating a local-stratum internal time source design
Configured node1 chrony.conf: removed public pool lines, added 'allow 10.100.254.0/24' and 'local stratum 10'
Disabled systemd-timesyncd and enabled/started chrony on node1; verified chronyd listening on 0.0.0.0:123 and tracking shows local stratum 10 reference
Configured node2 chrony.conf: removed public pool lines, added 'server 10.100.254.10 iburst prefer'
Disabled systemd-timesyncd and enabled/started chrony on node2; verified node2's active source is node1 (stratum 11, Reference ID 0A64FE0A)
Verified node1's 'chronyc clients' shows NTP requests served to node2, confirming bidirectional internal sync
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, chrony active status, tracking/sources) on both nodes

Restarted node1 via native 'reboot' (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and uptime reset, confirmed chrony auto-started and returned to local stratum 10
Confirmed node2 remained synced to node1 across node1's restart

Restarted node2 via native 'reboot', polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id and uptime reset, confirmed chrony auto-started and node2 automatically re-synced to node1 (stratum 11) post-reboot
Final cross-check: node1 'chronyc clients' shows continued NTP requests from node2 after both restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as internal time source (self-referenced local stratum, serving cluster subnet)
evidence.summary: chrony.conf on node1 stripped of public pools, 'allow 10.100.254.0/24' and 'local stratum 10' added; chronyc tracking shows Stratum 10 self-reference; ss shows chronyd listening on 0.0.0.0:123

evidence.requirement: node2 configured to sync against node1 instead of public NTP
evidence.summary: chrony.conf on node2 stripped of public pools, 'server 10.100.254.10 iburst prefer' added; chronyc sources -v shows '^*' active sync to 10.100.254.10 at stratum 11 within seconds of chrony start

evidence.requirement: bidirectional confirmation node2 actually queries node1
evidence.summary: chronyc clients on node1 shows 4 NTP requests received from node2's IP

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline before restart (boot identity + service/data health)
evidence.summary: node1 boot_id=1e0cb179-d384-41f8-aa25-9390b31eec45, uptime~93s, chrony active, tracking stratum 10

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline before restart (boot identity + service/data health)
evidence.summary: node2 boot_id=29011044-5356-46eb-ba9c-1470170355a7, uptime~94s, chrony active, source ^* node1

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: backgrounded reboot command acknowledged immediately; next call returned connection timed out, proving disconnect occurred after ack

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity after restart (proof of actual reboot)
evidence.summary: node reachable again; boot_id changed to 50b469b0-5bd4-43d2-8d35-34fc04169e69 (from 1e0cb179...), uptime reset to ~5.8s

evidence.requirement: node1 recovered service/data state after restart
evidence.summary: chrony active again on node1 with local stratum 10 restored; node2 confirmed still synced to node1 (^*, stratum 11) after node1's restart, proving cluster time hierarchy recovered

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: backgrounded reboot command acknowledged immediately; subsequent call returned connection reset/timeout, proving disconnect occurred after ack

evidence.requirement: node2 changed boot identity after restart (proof of actual reboot)
evidence.summary: node reachable again; boot_id changed to 8b97d254-e71e-4d16-bb13-3d6344195ca1 (from 29011044...), uptime reset to ~6.1s

evidence.requirement: node2 recovered service/data state and cluster sync after restart
evidence.summary: chrony active again on node2 and automatically re-synced to node1 (^*, stratum 11, Reference ID 0A64FE0A) without manual intervention; node1's chronyc clients confirms continued NTP requests from node2 post-restart
